ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, X on the left is used as a common input and is connected respectively to the four AND gates on the right; the outputs of the four AND gates on the right are labeled from top to bottom as P0, P1, P2, P3. At the top there are select signals S1 and S0, and each select signal has both the original signal and the inverted signal lines, which are respectively sent to different AND-gate select inputs. Reasoning: Substitute S1 = 0, S0 = 1, then NOT S1 = 1, S0 = 1. Only the AND gate connected to the two select inputs NOT S1 and S0 will be enabled, and its output equals the common input X. According to the wiring in the figure, this enabled AND gate corresponds to output P1, so P1 = X.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: X is a common input bus into all four AND gates, while S1 and S0 are routed as true/complement select lines to different gates. From the text, substitute S1=0 and S0=1. Evaluate the select literals on each gate: the gate connected to not-S1 and S0 has both select inputs high, so its output follows X. In the diagram that gate is labeled P1, hence P1 = X.
